# ADARE test-function catalog

Reference a test from a playbook `tests:` block by its dotnotation. Required parameters are marked **bold**. Search instead of scrolling: `adare test search "<goal>"`.

## csv

### `csv.compare_files`

compares two CSV files with full diff reporting

**Use for:** diffing a produced CSV against a reference CSV available on the same machine. For inline expectations use csv.compare_rows. Needs the in-guest agent: agentless host mode only pulls a ``dst`` parameter, and this function has none.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| actual | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the CSV under test; a glob must match exactly one path, a missing or ambiguous file (or a CSV parse error) is an error. |
| reference | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the reference CSV, resolved like ``actual``. |
| columns | `list[int]` | `None` | 0-based column indices to compare; ``None`` compares all columns. |
| ignore_order | `bool` | `False` | ``False`` (default) compares row N with row N; ``True`` matches rows as a multiset. |
| allow_extra_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on rows only in ``actual`` (ordered mode: trailing rows only). |
| allow_missing_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on rows only in ``reference`` (ordered mode: trailing rows only). |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name (``cp1252``) reads BOM-less files (both) with it. A BOM always wins. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_compare_files
  function: csv.compare_files
  parameter:
    actual: <str>
    reference: <str>
```

### `csv.compare_rows`

compares all rows in CSV against embedded reference data

**Use for:** asserting a whole (small) CSV export. To compare against a second CSV file use csv.compare_files.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the CSV file. A glob must match exactly one path; no/ambiguous match, a missing file or a CSV parse error is an error. Default ``csv`` dialect; header row included. |
| reference_rows | `list[list[str]]` | `None` | Expected rows, a non-empty list of lists of strings (quote numbers in YAML). ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags are matched by type; other cells exactly. |
| columns | `list[int]` | `None` | 0-based column indices to compare (others ignored; out-of-range indices are silently dropped). ``None`` compares all columns. |
| ignore_order | `bool` | `False` | ``False`` (default) compares row N with row N; ``True`` matches rows as a multiset regardless of position. |
| allow_extra_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on actual rows without a reference counterpart (in ordered mode only trailing rows count as extra). |
| allow_missing_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on reference rows missing from the file (in ordered mode only trailing rows count as missing). |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name (``cp1252``) reads BOM-less files with it. A BOM always wins. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_compare_rows
  function: csv.compare_rows
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `csv.contains_line`

tests if row in a csv file exists that matches the given entry layout

**Use for:** checking a tool's CSV output (e.g. a timeline) contains a specific record.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the CSV file. A glob must match exactly one path; no/ambiguous match, a missing file or a CSV parse error is an error. Parsed with the default ``csv`` dialect (comma, double quotes); the header row is a normal row. |
| entry | `list` | `None` | Expected row as a list, one item per column; a row must have exactly this many columns. Items are compared as exact, case-sensitive strings (``str(item)``), or by type for ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags (``!re`` uses ``re.match``, anchored at the start). Required in practice: omitting it is an execution error unless the file is empty. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name (``cp1252``) reads BOM-less files with it. A BOM always wins. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_line
  function: csv.contains_line
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `csv.row_count`

tests the number of rows (records) in a CSV file that match the given entry layout

**Use for:** asserting how often a record occurs (exactly one row for a file); absence of a row: ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` on csv.contains_line). Counts CSV records, so a quoted field with a line break is one row; for physical lines use text.line_count, for JSON Lines records jsonl.line_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the CSV file. A glob must match exactly one path; no/ambiguous match, a missing file, undecodable content or a CSV parse error is an error. Parsed like csv.contains_line (default ``csv`` dialect; the header row is a normal row). |
| **entry** | `list` |  | Expected row as a list, matched exactly like csv.contains_line: one item per column (a row with another column count never matches), exact case-sensitive strings or ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags. A non-list is an error. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name (``cp1252``) reads BOM-less files with it. A BOM always wins. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_row_count
  function: csv.row_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    entry: <list>
    expected_count: <int>
```

## excel

### `excel.cell_value_matches`

validates specific cell value with placeholder support

**Use for:** asserting one value a user typed or a formula result saved in a workbook. Cells are read via pandas and stringified: empty -> ``''``; numbers via ``str()`` (an int may read as ``5.0`` if pandas upcasts the column/row to float); dates as ``2024-01-31 00:00:00`` or ``2024-01-31T00:00:00`` depending on the row's other cells -- use ``!re`` for dates and numbers when unsure.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the .xlsx; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing or unreadable file is an error. |
| row | `int` | `0` | 0-based row index in the raw sheet (row 0 = spreadsheet row 1); out of range fails. |
| column | `int` | `0` | 0-based column index (A = 0); out of range fails. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Compared exactly with ``str(expected_value)`` (``None`` -> ``''``). A single ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag is matched by type. |
| sheet | `str \| int` | `0` | Sheet name (str) or 0-based sheet index (int); unknown sheets fail. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat ``expected_value`` as a regex searched in the cell value (``re.search``, unanchored; ``^...$`` for the whole value); an invalid regex is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_cell_value_matches
  function: excel.cell_value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `excel.compare_files`

compares entire Excel files with multi-sheet awareness

**Use for:** whole-workbook comparison. Needs the in-guest agent (agentless host mode only pulls a ``dst`` parameter).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| actual | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the workbook under test; glob must match exactly one path. |
| reference | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the reference workbook. |
| sheet_mode | `str` | `'by_name'` | ``by_name`` (default; pair equal names), ``by_index`` (pair by position) or ``specific`` (only ``specific_sheets`` present in both; extra sheets ignored). Other values are an error. |
| specific_sheets | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Sheet names for ``specific`` mode; names absent from ``actual`` count as missing, names absent only from ``reference`` are skipped. Empty passes vacuously. |
| columns | `list[int] \| None` | `None` | 0-based column indices to compare; ``None`` compares all. |
| ignore_order | `bool` | `False` | ``True`` matches rows as a multiset instead of position by position. |
| allow_extra_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on extra actual rows (ordered mode: trailing rows only). |
| allow_missing_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on missing reference rows (ordered mode: trailing only). |
| allow_extra_sheets | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on sheets only in ``actual``. |
| allow_missing_sheets | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on sheets only in ``reference``. |
| header_row | `int \| None` | `None` | Number of top rows to skip in every sheet. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_compare_files
  function: excel.compare_files
  parameter:
    actual: <str>
    reference: <str>
```

**Use for:** asserting sheet contents. Give exactly one of ``reference_rows``/``reference_file`` (both or neither fails). Cells are stringified as in excel.cell_value_matches.

| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the .xlsx under test; a glob must match exactly one path. |
| reference_rows | `list[list[str]] \| None` | `None` | Expected rows as a list of lists of strings; ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags allowed. |

| reference_sheet | `str \| int` | `0` | Sheet name or 0-based index in ``reference_file``. |
| reference_header_row | `int \| None` | `None` | Number of top rows to skip in ``reference_file``. |
| sheet | `str \| int` | `0` | Sheet name or 0-based index in ``dst``. |
| columns | `list[int] \| None` | `None` | 0-based column indices to compare; ``None`` compares all. |
| ignore_order | `bool` | `False` | ``True`` matches rows as a multiset instead of position by position. |
| allow_extra_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on extra actual rows (ordered mode: trailing rows only). |
| allow_missing_rows | `bool` | `False` | Do not fail on missing reference rows (ordered mode: trailing only). |
| header_row | `int \| None` | `None` | Number of top rows of ``dst`` to skip (not a row index). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_compare_rows
  function: excel.compare_rows
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `excel.row_count`

tests the number of rows in an Excel sheet that match the given entry layout

**Use for:** asserting how often a record occurs (exactly one row for an item); absence of a row: ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` on excel.contains_row).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the .xlsx; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing or unreadable file is an error. |
| **entry** | `list` |  | Expected row as a list, matched exactly like excel.contains_row: one item per column of the sheet's used width (a row with another width never matches), exact strings or ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags. A non-list is an error. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| sheet | `str \| int` | `0` | Sheet name (str) or 0-based index (int); an unknown sheet fails, like excel.contains_row. |
| header_row | `int \| None` | `None` | Number of top rows to skip before counting; ``None`` skips none. A negative number or a non-integer is an error. |

```yaml
tests:

  function: excel.row_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    entry: <list>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `image.dimensions_match`

tests if an image has the expected width and/or height in pixels

**Use for:** checking an exported, resized or cropped image, or a generated thumbnail.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the image (any format Pillow reads); a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or a file that is not an image is an error. |
| width | `int` | `None` | Expected width in pixels (positive integer). |
| height | `int` | `None` | Expected height in pixels (positive integer). Give at least one of the two; neither, or a non-positive / non-integer value, is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_dimensions_match
  function: image.dimensions_match
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `image.exif_value_count`

tests the number of occurrences of an EXIF tag (optionally with a matching value)

**Use for:** absence: ``expected_count: 0`` asserts the tag was not written (or stripped, e.g. location data removed on export).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the image; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file, a file that is not an image or has corrupt EXIF data is an error. |
| **tag** | `str \| int` |  | Tag name (``Make``, ``GPSLatitude``) or number (``0x010f``); names are looked up in their IFD (IFD0 + Exif IFD, or GPS IFD), numbers in all three, and each IFD that has the tag counts once. An unknown name is an error. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Required non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Count only occurrences whose value text equals/matches this (same formatting as image.exif_value_matches); ``None`` (default) counts every occurrence. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_exif_value_count
  function: image.exif_value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    tag: <str | int>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `image.exif_value_matches`

tests if an EXIF tag (IFD0, Exif or GPS IFD) equals or matches an expected value

**Use for:** camera, time and location metadata written into photos (JPEG, PNG eXIf, TIFF, WebP). A tag present in several IFDs passes if one occurrence matches (``wildcard_mode: all``: every occurrence must match); a missing tag fails. For "absent" use image.exif_value_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the image; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file, a file that is not an image or has corrupt EXIF data is an error. |
| **tag** | `str \| int` |  | Tag name as in Pillow's tables (``Make``, ``DateTimeOriginal``, ``GPSLatitude``) or a number (``0x9003``, ``36867``). Main-table names are looked up in IFD0 and the Exif IFD, GPS names in the GPS IFD, numbers in all three. An unknown name is an error. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool` |  | Compared with the value's text form: text as stored (trailing NULs removed); integers in decimal; rationals and floats as decimals (``72``, ``2.8``, ``0.004``; ``nan`` for x/0); sequences joined with ``", "`` (GPS ``51, 30, 12.5``); bytes as text when printable UTF-8, else lowercase hex; the user comment without its 8-byte charset prefix; the UTF-16 title/comment tags (0x9C9B-0x9C9F) decoded. A YAML number is formatted the same way (write a sequence as text, ``51, 30, 12.5``); a ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag or ``{{placeholder}}`` is matched by type. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | With the tag in several IFDs, ``any`` (default): one occurrence must match; ``all``: every one must match. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_exif_value_matches
  function: image.exif_value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    tag: <str | int>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool>
```

### `image.png_text_count`

tests the number of PNG text chunks with a keyword (optionally with a matching text)

**Use for:** duplicate keywords and absence: ``expected_count: 0`` asserts no such chunk (or none with that text).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the PNG file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file, a bad signature, a truncated chunk, any chunk CRC mismatch, a malformed or undecompressable text chunk, or a missing IEND is an error. |
| **keyword** | `str` |  | Chunk keyword, compared exactly; tEXt, zTXt and iTXt chunks are counted together, also those after the image data. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Required non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Count only chunks whose text equals/matches this (same rules as image.png_text_matches); ``None`` (default) counts every chunk with ``keyword``. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_png_text_count
  function: image.png_text_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    keyword: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `image.png_text_matches`

tests if a PNG text chunk (tEXt/zTXt/iTXt) with a keyword exists or matches an expected value

**Use for:** metadata an application embeds in saved images (software, source, comment). With several chunks for ``keyword``, one match is enough (``wildcard_mode: all``: every chunk must match). For "absent" use image.png_text_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the PNG file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file, a bad signature, a truncated chunk, any chunk CRC mismatch, a malformed or undecompressable text chunk, or a missing IEND is an error. |
| **keyword** | `str` |  | Chunk keyword, compared exactly (case-sensitive). All chunks up to IEND are read, also those after the image data. tEXt is Latin-1, zTXt zlib + Latin-1, iTXt UTF-8 (compressed or not; language tag and translated keyword are ignored). |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default): the keyword exists. Otherwise compared with the text; a YAML number/boolean is compared as its text, a ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag or ``{{placeholder}}`` is matched by type. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | With several chunks for ``keyword``, ``any`` (default): one must match; ``all``: every one must match. Ignored without ``expected_value``. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_png_text_matches
  function: image.png_text_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    keyword: <str>
```

## ini

### `ini.contains_key`

tests if an INI file contains a key in a section

**Use for:** checking a setting was written, whatever its value. For "absent" use ini.value_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the INI file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing, unreadable or undecodable file is an error. |
| **section** | `str` |  | Section name without brackets; ``''`` = keys before the first header. Duplicate sections are searched together. |
| **key** | `str` |  | Key name, compared after stripping. The first ``=`` on a line splits key and value; lines without ``=`` are ignored, so a bare word is not a key. |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares section and key names case-insensitively. |
| encoding | `str` | `None` | Text encoding; default auto: a BOM wins, BOM-less UTF-16 is recognised, everything else is read as UTF-8. An unknown name is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: ini.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    section: <str>
    key: <str>
```

### `ini.section_exists`

tests if an INI file contains a section

**Use for:** checking a settings file gained a section. For "absent" use ``expect_to_fail`` (or ini.value_count with ``expected_count: 0`` for a key).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the INI file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing, unreadable or undecodable file is an error. |
| **section** | `str` |  | Section name without brackets, compared after stripping. Keys before the first header belong to section ``''``, which exists only as a header ``[]``. |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares section names case-insensitively. |
| encoding | `str` | `None` | Text encoding; default auto: a BOM wins, BOM-less UTF-16 is recognised, everything else is read as UTF-8. An unknown name is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_section_exists
  function: ini.section_exists
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    section: <str>
```

### `ini.value_count`

tests the number of occurrences of an INI key (optionally with a matching value)

**Use for:** duplicate keys (lists written as repeated keys) and absence: ``expected_count: 0`` asserts the key (or the key with that value) is not in the section.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the INI file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing, unreadable or undecodable file is an error. |
| **section** | `str` |  | Section name without brackets; ``''`` = keys before the first header. Occurrences in duplicate sections are added up. |
| **key** | `str` |  | Key name; the first ``=`` on a line splits key and value. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Required non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Count only occurrences whose raw value equals/matches this (same rules as ini.value_matches); ``None`` (default) counts every occurrence. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares section and key names case-insensitively. |
| encoding | `str` | `None` | Text encoding; default auto (BOM, BOM-less UTF-16, else UTF-8). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: ini.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    section: <str>
    key: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `ini.value_matches`

tests if an INI value equals or matches an expected value (regex and placeholders supported)

**Use for:** asserting a setting's value. With duplicate keys or sections, one matching occurrence is enough (``wildcard_mode: all``: every occurrence must match). A missing key fails.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the INI file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing, unreadable or undecodable file is an error. |
| **section** | `str` |  | Section name without brackets; ``''`` = keys before the first header. |
| **key** | `str` |  | Key name; the first ``=`` on a line splits key and value. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool` |  | Compared with the raw value text (stripped; quotes and inline comments are kept, ``a = "x" ; note`` has the value ``"x" ; note``). A YAML number or boolean is compared as its text (``8080``, ``true``/``false``). A ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag or ``{{placeholder}}`` is matched by type. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). An invalid regex is an error. |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares section and key names case-insensitively; values are always compared as given. |
| encoding | `str` | `None` | Text encoding; default auto (BOM, BOM-less UTF-16, else UTF-8). |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | With several occurrences, ``any`` (default): one must match; ``all``: every one must match. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: ini.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    section: <str>
    key: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool>
```

## json

### `json.array_contains`

tests if JSON array at specified path contains expected element

**Use for:** checking that a list in a JSON file includes an entry. To count entries use json.value_count (``array_path[*]`` as key path).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the JSON file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or invalid JSON is an error; an unresolvable path or non-array value fails. ``x.jsonlz4!`` reads LZ4-compressed JSON. |
| **array_path** | `str` |  | Dot path to the array (same syntax as json.value_matches ``key_path``); a wildcard yielding several values is treated as the array of those values. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| dict \| list \| None` |  | Required. An element equal to it (type-sensitive ``==``; dicts and lists must match exactly). A ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag passes if any element's ``str()`` matches; an invalid regex or unknown placeholder is an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects UTF-8/16/32 with or without BOM; a name (``latin-1``) decodes BOM-less files with it. Unknown names are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_array_contains
  function: json.array_contains
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    array_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | dict | list | None>
```

### `json.contains_key`

tests if JSON file contains specified key path (supports dot notation like "user.profile.name")

**Use for:** checking a settings/config file gained a key. To also check the value use json.value_matches. Absence of a key: ``expect_to_fail: true`` here, or json.value_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the JSON file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or invalid JSON is an error. LZ4-compressed JSON is read through the archive separator (``/home/user/data/store.jsonlz4!``). |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root, e.g. ``user.profile.name``. ``*`` expands all values of an object (``config.*.enabled``), ``[*]`` all elements of an array (``users[*].email``), ``[n]`` one element (``items[0]``; ``items[-1]`` = last). A leading bracket addresses a top-level array (``[0].name``, ``[*].id``); ``['a.b']`` quotes a key that contains dots or brackets. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects UTF-8/16/32 with or without BOM; a name (``latin-1``) decodes BOM-less files with it. Unknown names are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: json.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `json.value_count`

tests the number of JSON values at a key path (optionally only those matching a value)

**Use for:** counting entries (e.g. exactly 3 bookmarks with a given tag) and asserting absence: ``expected_count: 0`` without ``expected_value`` passes when the key path selects nothing, with ``expected_value`` when no value matches. To check what one value is use json.value_matches.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the JSON file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or invalid JSON is an error. ``x.jsonlz4!`` reads LZ4-compressed JSON. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root, e.g. ``user.profile.name``. ``*`` expands all values of an object (``config.*.enabled``), ``[*]`` all elements of an array (``users[*].email``), ``[n]`` one element (``items[0]``; ``items[-1]`` = last). A leading bracket addresses a top-level array (``[0].name``, ``[*].id``); ``['a.b']`` quotes a key that contains dots or brackets. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) counts the values the path selects (a ``null`` value counts; an array is one value, ``items[*]`` counts its elements). Otherwise counts the values equal to it (type-sensitive ``==``; ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags compare ``str(value)``; an invalid regex or unknown placeholder is an error); a path that selects exactly one array compares its elements one by one. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``; an invalid regex is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects UTF-8/16/32 with or without BOM; a name (``latin-1``) decodes BOM-less files with it. Unknown names are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: json.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `json.value_matches`

tests if JSON value at key path matches expected value using placeholders (supports wildcards [*] and * with any/all modes)

**Use for:** asserting a setting/field value. If the path yields several values (a wildcard, or a JSON array value, whose elements are then compared one by one) ``wildcard_mode`` decides; a one-element array is unwrapped. Whole arrays cannot be compared. To assert that no value matches use json.value_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the JSON file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or invalid JSON is an error; an unresolvable key path fails. ``x.jsonlz4!`` reads LZ4-compressed JSON. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root, e.g. ``user.profile.name``. ``*`` expands all values of an object (``config.*.enabled``), ``[*]`` all elements of an array (``users[*].email``), ``[n]`` one element (``items[0]``; ``items[-1]`` = last). A leading bracket addresses a top-level array (``[0].name``, ``[*].id``); ``['a.b']`` quotes a key that contains dots or brackets. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` |  | Required. Compared with Python ``==``, which is type-sensitive (``5`` != ``"5"``; a JSON ``null`` needs ``expected_value: null``). A ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag compares ``str(value)`` by type; an invalid regex or unknown placeholder is an error. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default): one value must match; ``all``: every value must match. Other values are an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects UTF-8/16/32 with or without BOM; a name (``latin-1``) decodes BOM-less files with it. Unknown names are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: json.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | None>
```

## jsonl

### `jsonl.line_count`

counts lines in JSONL file matching conditions and validates against expected count (if None, requires at least 1 match)

**Use for:** asserting how many records/events were written (e.g. exactly 3 deletions); absence: ``expected_count: 0``. For CSV records use csv.row_count, for lines of a plain text file text.line_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the JSONL file (one JSON document per line; blank lines are skipped). A glob must match exactly one path; a missing file is an error, a 0-byte file has 0 lines (passes ``expected_count: 0``). |
| conditions | `dict[str, str \| int \| float \| bool \| None] \| None` | `None` | Mapping ``key_path -> expected value`` (all must hold; for multi-value paths one matching element suffices). ``None``/empty counts every valid JSON line. |
| expected_count | `int \| dict[str, int] \| None` | `None` | Non-negative ``int`` compared with ``comparison_type``, ``{min: N, max: M}`` for a range (either bound optional: min defaults to 0, max to unbounded), or ``None`` for "at least 1". Anything else (a negative number, a boolean, other keys, min > max) is an error. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat string expected values as regexes searched (``re.search``) in ``str(value)``; the value ``"*"`` then means "key exists". Without it, values are compared with type-sensitive ``==``; ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags always work. |
| skip_malformed | `bool` | `True` | ``True`` (default) ignores lines that are not valid JSON; ``False`` makes the first malformed line an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``, applied to an ``int`` ``expected_count``. With the range form or ``None`` only ``equals`` is allowed; other values are an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name reads BOM-less files with it. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_line_count
  function: jsonl.line_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `jsonl.line_matches`

tests if lines in JSONL file match specified conditions (supports any/all modes)

**Use for:** event logs / NDJSON exports (e.g. "a line with type=login and user=alice exists"). To count matches use jsonl.line_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the JSONL file (one JSON document per line; blank lines are skipped). A glob must match exactly one path; a missing file is an error, a 0-byte file fails. |
| conditions | `dict[str, str \| int \| float \| bool \| None]` | `None` | Required mapping ``key_path -> expected value``; a line matches when every condition holds. If a path yields several values (wildcard or JSON array), one matching element suffices. Missing keys fail the line. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default) or ``all`` (every valid line must match; no valid lines fails). Other values are an error. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat string expected values as regexes searched (``re.search``) in ``str(value)``; the value ``"*"`` then means "key exists". Without it, values are compared with type-sensitive ``==``; ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags always work. |
| skip_malformed | `bool` | `True` | ``True`` (default) ignores lines that are not valid JSON; ``False`` makes the first malformed line an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name reads BOM-less files with it. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_line_matches
  function: jsonl.line_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `jsonl.value_in_any_line`

tests if specified key path with expected value exists in any line of JSONL file

**Use for:** a single-field check across a log; for multi-field conditions use jsonl.line_matches.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the JSONL file (one JSON document per line; blank lines are skipped). A glob must match exactly one path; a missing file is an error, a 0-byte file fails. |
| key_path | `str` | `''` | Dot path inside each line's object, e.g. ``event.type``; ``*`` expands object values, ``name[*]`` array elements. No numeric indexes. For multi-value paths one matching element suffices. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Value to find; see ``regex_match`` for how it is compared. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat string expected values as regexes searched (``re.search``) in ``str(value)``; the value ``"*"`` then means "key exists". Without it, values are compared with type-sensitive ``==``; ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags always work. |
| skip_malformed | `bool` | `True` | ``True`` (default) ignores lines that are not valid JSON; ``False`` makes the first malformed line an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8; a name reads BOM-less files with it. Unknown names or undecodable content are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_in_any_line
  function: jsonl.value_in_any_line
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `linux.log_entry_exists`

tests if one of the last lines of a text log contains a string or matches a regex

**Use for:** checking an action left a trace in a plain-text log (syslog, auth.log, app logs; not the binary journal). To count entries, or to search the whole file, use text.line_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: linux

| parameter | type | default | description |

The encoding is detected (BOM, UTF-16, else UTF-8); undecodable bytes are replaced, so binary garbage does not stop the search. |
| **content** | `str` |  | With ``regex_match`` (default) a Python regex searched in each line (``re.search``, case-sensitive; ``(?i)`` for case-insensitive); an invalid regex is an error. Otherwise a substring a line must contain. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `True` | ``True`` (default): ``content`` is a regex; ``False``: a plain substring. |
| max_lines | `int` | `1000` | How many trailing lines to search (default 1000); must be positive. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_log_entry_exists
  function: linux.log_entry_exists
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    content: <str>
```

**Use for:** checking a systemd unit was started/stopped by an action. Linux guests only (other OSes, a missing ``systemctl`` or a 10 s timeout are execution errors).

*QGA_PROBE*, os: linux

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|

| **expected_status** | `str` |  | Exact, case-sensitive ``is-active`` output: ``active``, ``inactive``, ``failed``, ``activating``, ``deactivating`` ... (unknown units usually print ``inactive``). |

## plist

### `plist.contains_key`

tests if a property list (XML or binary plist) contains the specified key path

**Use for:** checking that a preferences/settings plist gained a key. To also check the value use plist.value_matches; to check that a key is absent use plist.value_count with ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` here: a missing file stays an error).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the plist; XML and binary plists are detected from the content. A glob must match exactly one path; ``archive.zip!/member.plist`` reads an archive member. A missing, unreadable or invalid file is an error. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root dictionary, e.g. ``window.frame``. Keys that contain dots use quotes in brackets (``['com.example.lastVersion']``, also mid-path: ``recent['com.example.doc'].name``). ``*`` expands all values of a dictionary, ``name[*]`` all elements of array ``name``, ``name[0]`` / ``name[-1]`` one element; a leading ``[0]`` / ``[*]`` addresses a top-level array. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: plist.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `plist.value_count`

tests how many property list values exist at a key path, optionally only those matching a value (0 = absent)

**Use for:** counting entries (``recent[*]``) and asserting absence: ``expected_count: 0`` passes when the key path selects nothing (or nothing matches ``expected_value``), while a missing or invalid file is still an error. A path that selects one array counts its elements when ``expected_value`` is given; without it every selected value counts once.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the plist (XML or binary, detected from the content); a glob must match exactly one path. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root dictionary (syntax as in plist.contains_key). |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare with. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Only count values equal to this (normalised as in plist.value_matches: dates are ISO strings, data is hex). ``None`` (default) counts every value. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched in ``str(value)``. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: plist.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `plist.value_matches`

tests if the property list value at a key path matches the expected value (dates as ISO strings, data as hex)

**Use for:** asserting a preference value. If the path yields several values (a wildcard, or an array value, whose elements are then compared one by one) ``wildcard_mode`` decides. Values are normalised before comparing: ``<date>`` becomes an ISO 8601 string without zone (plist dates are UTC, ``2024-01-15T10:30:00``), ``<data>`` a lowercase hex string (``0a1b``), ``<integer>``/``<real>``/``<true/>`` stay numbers and booleans.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the plist (XML or binary, detected from the content); a glob must match exactly one path. A missing or invalid file is an error; an unresolvable key path fails. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root dictionary; ``['com.example.key']`` for keys with dots, ``*`` all values of a dictionary, ``name[*]`` / ``name[0]`` array elements, a leading ``[0]`` / ``[*]`` for a top-level array. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` |  | Compared with Python ``==``, which is type-sensitive (``5`` != ``"5"``). A ``!re`` tag (``re.match``) or ``{{placeholder}}`` compares ``str(value)``. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``. An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default): one value must match; ``all``: every value must match. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: plist.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | None>
```

## sqlite

### `sqlite.query_result`

executes SQL query against SQLite database and validates result

**Use for:** asserting that a row was written, changed or removed. The original file is never opened: ``dst`` and any ``-wal``/``-journal`` sidecar are copied to a temp dir and the copy is queried, so uncheckpointed changes are seen and the evidence is not modified. Details report ``queried snapshot: <file> sha256=...`` per copied file and, once the query ran, the rows read (``query result: [...]``, also on success). With neither expectation set, it passes whenever the query runs. To only count rows use sqlite.row_count. Timestamps stored as numbers (Unix seconds, microseconds since 1601) are compared with ``!timestamp`` and its ``epoch``/``unit`` options.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the database; a glob must match exactly one file (otherwise an error). A missing file is an error. |
| **query** | `str` |  | SQL to execute, e.g. ``SELECT name FROM items WHERE name LIKE '%example%'``. A SQL error (syntax, unknown table, unreadable database) is an error. |
| expected_count | `int \| None` | `None` | Number of rows the query must return, compared with ``comparison_type``; ``None`` skips the check. Use ``0`` to assert a row is gone. A negative number or a non-integer is an error. |
| expected_result | `list \| None` | `None` | Exact expected rows as a list of ``{column: value}`` mappings, in query order; ``None`` skips the check. Placeholders compare the stringified result. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal`` for ``expected_count``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_query_result
  function: sqlite.query_result
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    query: <str>
```

### `sqlite.row_count`

tests the number of rows an SQL query returns on an SQLite database

**Use for:** asserting how many records an action left behind (exactly one history entry for a URL); asserting a record is gone: ``expected_count: 0``. Queried like sqlite.query_result: ``dst`` and any ``-wal``/``-journal`` sidecar are copied to a temp dir and the copy is queried, so uncheckpointed changes are seen and the evidence is not modified. Details report the count, the rows read (``query result: [...]``) and ``queried snapshot: <file> sha256=...`` per copied file. To check the row contents use sqlite.query_result with ``expected_result``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the database; a glob must match exactly one file (otherwise an error). A missing file is an error. |
| **query** | `str` |  | SQL to execute, e.g. ``SELECT id FROM items WHERE name = 'example'``; every returned row counts (``SELECT COUNT(*)`` returns one row). A SQL error (syntax, unknown table, unreadable database) is an error. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_row_count
  function: sqlite.row_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    query: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

## standard

### `standard.dir_content`

tests if a directory has the expected files/folders

**Use for:** checking a folder contains expected files/subfolders. Extra entries are allowed (only listed in the failure details); the listing is not recursive.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the directory. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing or unreadable directory is an execution error, not a failure. |
| files | `list` | `None` | Entry names (not paths) that must be present, compared exactly and case-sensitively against the directory listing. ``None``/empty always passes. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_dir_content
  function: standard.dir_content
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `standard.dir_does_not_exist`

tests if directory(ies) with path destination(dst) do NOT exist (supports glob patterns with match_mode)

**Use for:** verifying a folder was removed or never created. Opposite: standard.dir_exists. A regular file at ``dst`` does not count as a directory, so it passes.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path; glob characters ``* ? [ ]`` expanded with Python ``glob`` (not recursive). |
| match_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default; anything except ``single``): passes when zero matches are directories. ``single``: a glob must match exactly one path, else the test ERRORS -- a glob with no matches errors instead of passing. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_dir_does_not_exist
  function: standard.dir_does_not_exist
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `standard.dir_exists`

tests if directory(ies) with path destination(dst) exist (supports glob patterns with match_mode)

**Use for:** verifying an install/extract step created a folder. Opposite: standard.dir_does_not_exist.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the directory; glob characters ``* ? [ ]`` expanded with Python ``glob`` (not recursive). A path that exists but is a file fails. |
| match_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default; anything except ``single``): passes if one match is a directory. ``single``: a glob must match exactly one path, else the test ERRORS. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_dir_exists
  function: standard.dir_exists
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `standard.file_content_contains`

tests if file content contains specified string or byte pattern

**Use for:** checking a value/marker was written into a file. For patterns use standard.file_content_matches_regex; to count occurrences, search several encodings at once or assert a value is gone from a binary file use text.occurrence_count.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing file is an error. |
| content | `str` | `''` | Text to find (case-sensitive). An empty value always passes. In ``bytes`` mode ASCII characters stand for their byte and Python escapes (``\x00``, ``\n``, ``\\``) are decoded; a non-ASCII character or an unknown escape is an error (write ``\xNN``, or use ``string`` mode with an ``encoding``). |
| content_type | `str` | `'string'` | ``string`` (default) searches the decoded text, ``bytes`` the raw file bytes; other values are an error. A ``!re``/``!timestamp`` placeholder in ``content`` is an error (use standard.file_content_matches_regex). |
| encoding | `str` | `'utf-8'` | Codec for ``string`` mode; undecodable bytes are silently dropped. ``BOM`` detects UTF-8/16/32 from the byte-order mark and errors if there is none. |
| strip_bom | `bool` | `False` | Remove a leading U+FEFF from the decoded text (``string`` mode only). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_content_contains
  function: standard.file_content_contains
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    content: <str>
```

### `standard.file_content_equals`

tests if file content equals the given content

**Use for:** exact output checks, e.g. a tool's exit code or a saved text document. That a file is empty: standard.file_size with ``expected_size: 0``.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing file is an error; a failure includes a unified diff. |
| content | `str` | `''` | Expected text. Both sides are ``strip()``-ed; inner whitespace must match (line endings are normalised to ``\n`` by text-mode reading). ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tags inside the value become placeholders matched by type; the literal text around them must match exactly. |
| encoding | `str` | `'utf-8'` | Python codec used to decode the file (strict). ``BOM`` detects UTF-8/16/32 from the byte-order mark and errors if there is none. |
| strip_bom | `bool` | `False` | Remove a leading U+FEFF from the decoded text before comparing. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_content_equals
  function: standard.file_content_equals
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    content: <str>
```

### `standard.file_content_matches_regex`

tests if file content matches a given regex expression

**Use for:** loose content checks (a value appears, a line has a given shape). For exact content use standard.file_content_equals; for a plain substring standard.file_content_contains.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing file is an error. |
| regex | `str` | `''` | Python ``re`` pattern applied with ``re.search`` to the whole file. Default flags: case-sensitive, ``^``/``$`` match only file start/end; use inline flags such as ``(?im)``. An empty pattern always passes; an invalid one errors. |
| encoding | `str` | `'utf-8'` | Python codec used to decode the file (strict: undecodable bytes error). ``BOM`` detects UTF-8/16/32 from the byte-order mark and errors if there is none. |
| strip_bom | `bool` | `False` | Remove a leading U+FEFF from the decoded text before matching. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_content_matches_regex
  function: standard.file_content_matches_regex
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    regex: <str>
```

### `standard.file_count`

tests the number of files (or directories) matching a path or glob

**Use for:** how many files an application wrote (exactly 3 logs, at least one export) and absence of a whole group of files: ``expected_count: 0``. One file: standard.file_exists.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path or glob (Python ``glob``, not recursive: ``**`` acts like ``*``; ``*`` skips dotfiles), e.g. ``/home/user/logs/*.log``. No match counts 0, it is not an error; an empty ``dst`` or an unresolved ``{{placeholder}}`` is. Inside an archive (``a.zip!/logs/*.log``) the matching file members are counted; the archive itself must exist and be readable, otherwise an error. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| kind | `str` | `'file'` | ``file`` (default): regular files (also through a symlink); ``dir``: directories; ``any``: every existing path. Archives have file members only, so ``dir`` with an archive path is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_count
  function: standard.file_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `standard.file_does_not_exist`

tests if file(s) with path destination(dst) do NOT exist (supports glob patterns with match_mode)

**Use for:** verifying a file was deleted or never written. Opposite: standard.file_exists. A directory at ``dst`` does not count as a file, so it passes.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path; glob characters ``* ? [ ]`` expanded with Python ``glob`` (not recursive). Case sensitivity follows the guest filesystem. |
| match_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default; anything except ``single``): passes when zero matches are files. ``single``: a glob must match exactly one path, else the test ERRORS -- so a glob with no matches errors instead of passing; keep ``any`` for globs. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_does_not_exist
  function: standard.file_does_not_exist
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `standard.file_exists`

tests if file(s) with path destination(dst) exist (supports glob patterns with match_mode)

**Use for:** verifying a GUI action created/saved a file. Opposite: standard.file_does_not_exist. How many files match a glob: standard.file_count; an empty file: standard.file_size.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. Glob characters ``* ? [ ]`` are expanded with Python ``glob`` (not recursive: ``**`` acts like ``*``; ``*`` skips dotfiles), e.g. ``C:/Users/*/Desktop/*.txt``. Case sensitivity follows the guest filesystem. A path that exists but is a directory fails. |
| match_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default; any value except ``single`` behaves the same): passes if at least one match is a regular file. ``single``: a glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test ERRORS (not fails). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_exists
  function: standard.file_exists
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `standard.file_hash_matches`

tests if file hash matches expected value

**Use for:** verifying a file is byte-identical to a known artifact.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing file is an error. |
| expected_hash | `str` | `''` | Hex digest; compared case-insensitively but otherwise exactly (no whitespace stripping, no prefix such as ``sha256:``). |
| hash_type | `str` | `'sha256'` | ``md5``, ``sha1``, ``sha256`` (default) or ``sha512`` (case-insensitive); anything else is an execution error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_hash_matches
  function: standard.file_hash_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    expected_hash: <str>
```

### `standard.file_permissions`

tests file permissions, owner, and group

**Use for:** Unix mode/ownership checks after chmod/chown or a file save. Only meaningful on Linux guests: Windows reports synthetic mode bits and no owner/group (owner checks fail).

*QGA_PROBE*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file or directory. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing path is an error. |
| expected_permissions | `str` | `''` | Octal digits (``'644'``, ``'0755'``) or 9-char symbolic (``rwxr-xr-x``), compared with ``st_mode & 0o777`` (no setuid/sticky). Quote it in YAML (unquoted ``0644`` is read as decimal 420). Empty/invalid values error. |
| check_owner | `str` | `None` | Expected owner user name (not UID); ``None`` skips the check. |
| check_group | `str` | `None` | Expected group name (not GID); ``None`` skips the check. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_permissions
  function: standard.file_permissions
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    expected_permissions: <str>
```

### `standard.file_size`

tests the size of a file in bytes

**Use for:** checking a file is empty (``expected_size: 0``), non-empty (``greater`` 0) or grew/shrank past a threshold. Existence alone: standard.file_exists.

*FILE_BASED*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path; a missing file or a directory is an error. An archive member (``a.zip!/p/x.db``) has its extracted size. |
| **expected_size** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer number of bytes; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_size
  function: standard.file_size
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    expected_size: <int>
```

### `standard.file_timestamps`

tests file timestamps with various comparison types and formats

**Use for:** MACB timestamp assertions (modified recently, accessed after an action, ...).

*QGA_PROBE*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dst | `str` | `''` | Guest path to the file. A glob must match exactly one path, otherwise the test errors. A missing file is an error. |
| timestamp_type | `str` | `'modified'` | ``modified`` (mtime, default), ``accessed`` (atime) or ``created``: creation time on Windows; elsewhere ``st_birthtime`` if Python exposes it, else ``st_ctime`` (inode change time on Linux). Other values error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default, within ``tolerance_seconds``), ``before`` / ``after`` (strict, vs ``expected_time``), ``between`` (inclusive, ``start_time``.. ``end_time``) or ``within_last`` (``within_duration`` before the guest's now). |
| expected_time | `str \| int \| float` | `None` | Reference for equals/before/after: Unix epoch seconds or a date string (see ``time_format``). Naive strings are read in the guest's local timezone (the trailing ``Z`` format too). Missing/unparseable values error. |
| time_format | `str` | `None` | ``strptime`` format tried first; then ``%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S``, ``%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S``, ``%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ``, ``%Y-%m-%d``, ``%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S``, ``%m/%d/%Y``. |
| tolerance_seconds | `int` | `None` | Allowed absolute difference for ``equals``; ``None`` means 0, which rarely matches sub-second filesystem times. |
| start_time | `str \| int \| float` | `None` | Lower bound for ``between`` (same formats as ``expected_time``). |
| end_time | `str \| int \| float` | `None` | Upper bound for ``between``. |
| within_duration | `str` | `None` | For ``within_last``: integer plus unit ``s``/``m``/``h``/``d``, e.g. ``15m``. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_file_timestamps
  function: standard.file_timestamps
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

## text

### `text.line_count`

tests the number of text lines that contain a string or match a regex

**Use for:** counting log or history entries (exactly 2 lines with a file name); asserting a line is gone: ``expected_count: 0``. For binary files use text.occurrence_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the text file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or content not valid in the encoding is an error; an empty file has 0 lines. Lines end at ``\n``, ``\r\n`` or ``\r``. |
| **content** | `str` |  | Substring a line must contain (see ``case_sensitive``); an empty string counts every line. With ``regex_match`` a regex searched in each line (``re.search``); an invalid regex is an error. A ``!re`` or ``!timestamp`` placeholder is an error: write the pattern with ``regex_match``. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| encoding | `str \| None` | `None` | Text encoding; ``None`` (default) detects a BOM (UTF-8/16/32) and BOM-less UTF-16, else reads UTF-8. A BOM always wins. Unknown names are an error. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat ``content`` as a regex (see ``content``). |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``True`` (default) matches case exactly. ``False`` compares the substring after casefolding line and ``content`` (``Report`` = ``REPORT``, sharp s = ``ss``), or compiles the regex with ``re.IGNORECASE``. A non-boolean is an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_line_count
  function: text.line_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    content: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `text.occurrence_count`

tests how often a string or byte sequence occurs in a (text or binary) file

**Use for:** finding a value in any file, binary ones included (a database, a cache, a memory dump), in one or several encodings at once; asserting a value was wiped: ``expected_count: 0``. For line-based text use text.line_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file is an error. The raw bytes are searched, nothing is decoded. |
| **content** | `str` |  | What to find; must not be empty. Its meaning depends on ``content_type``. A ``!re`` or ``!timestamp`` placeholder is an error: for patterns use text.line_count with ``regex_match``. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| content_type | `str` | `'string'` | ``string`` (default): ``content`` encoded in each of ``encoding``. ``bytes``: ASCII characters stand for their byte, Python escapes (``\x00``, ``\n``, ``\\``) are decoded; a non-ASCII character or an unknown escape is an error (write ``\xNN``, or use ``string`` with an encoding). ``hex``: hex digits, whitespace allowed (``4d 5a 90 00``). |
| encoding | `list[str] \| str \| None` | `None` | Encoding(s) for ``string`` mode: one name (``utf-16-le``) or a list (default ``[utf-8]``), e.g. ``[utf-8, utf-16-le]``. Occurrences of the distinct encoded forms are summed (the same text stored once in each of two forms counts twice); a match on bytes already counted for an earlier form is skipped. ``utf-16``/``utf-32`` search both byte orders without BOM. Forms are matched at any byte offset, not aligned to characters. Unknown encodings, or ``content`` not encodable in one, are an error. |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` matches each character in any of its one-character case forms (``a``/``A``, ``ä``/``Ä``); case mappings to several characters (German sharp s to ``SS``) are not matched. ``string`` mode only, otherwise an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_occurrence_count
  function: text.occurrence_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    content: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

## toml

### `toml.contains_key`

tests if a TOML file contains the specified key path (tables, arrays of tables)

**Use for:** checking that a settings/config file gained a key. To also check the value use toml.value_matches; to check that a key is absent use toml.value_count with ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` here: a missing file stays an error).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the TOML file (UTF-8). A glob must match exactly one path; ``archive.zip!/member.toml`` reads an archive member. A missing, unreadable or invalid file is an error. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root table; ``[server]`` / ``server.port = 1`` are both ``server.port``. An array of tables (``[[items]]``) is an array: ``items[*].name`` for all entries, ``items[0].name`` / ``items[-1].name`` for one. ``*`` expands all values of a table (``profiles.*.enabled``). Keys with dots (quoted TOML keys such as ``"app.window"``) use quotes in brackets: ``['app.window'].width``. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: toml.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `toml.value_count`

tests how many TOML values exist at a key path, optionally only those matching a value (0 = absent)

**Use for:** counting entries (``items[*]`` for ``[[items]]``) and asserting absence: ``expected_count: 0`` passes when the key path selects nothing (or nothing matches ``expected_value``), while a missing or invalid file is still an error. A path that selects one array counts its elements when ``expected_value`` is given; without it every selected value counts once.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the TOML file; a glob must match exactly one path. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root table (syntax as in toml.contains_key). |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare with. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Only count values equal to this (normalised as in toml.value_matches). ``None`` (default) counts every value. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched in ``str(value)``. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: toml.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `toml.value_matches`

tests if the TOML value at a key path matches the expected value (dates/times as ISO strings)

**Use for:** asserting a setting/field value. If the path yields several values (a wildcard, or an array value, whose elements are then compared one by one) ``wildcard_mode`` decides. Values keep their TOML types (integers, floats, booleans, strings); dates and times become ISO 8601 strings: ``1979-05-27``, ``07:32:00``, ``1979-05-27T07:32:00`` (local) or ``1979-05-27T07:32:00-08:00`` (``Z`` becomes ``+00:00``).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the TOML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing or invalid file is an error; an unresolvable key path fails. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root table (syntax as in toml.contains_key), e.g. ``items[*].name`` for every ``[[items]]`` entry. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` |  | Compared with Python ``==``, which is type-sensitive (``5`` != ``"5"``). A ``!re`` tag (``re.match``) or ``{{placeholder}}`` compares ``str(value)``. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``. An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default): one value must match; ``all``: every value must match. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: toml.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | None>
```

## visual

### `visual.count_equals`

Check if text or image appears exactly N times on screen

**Use for:** counting visible items (e.g. 3 files on the desktop). Icon/image matches are capped at 10 by the CV call, so counts above 10 cannot be observed.

*HOST_NATIVE*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| text | `str` | `None` | OCR search string: case-insensitive substring of a single OCR text box (a phrase split across boxes may not match). Wins over ``icon`` and ``image``. |
| image | `str` | `None` | Template PNG on the HOST, relative to the playbook directory (or absolute); matched with the CV server's icon pipeline. A missing file is an execution error. |
| icon | `str` | `None` | Name from the icon library (``appdata/icon-library.yml``, e.g. ``recycle_bin``, ``folder``), extracted from the target on first use; needs a connected agent. Used when ``text`` is empty; wins over ``image``. |

```yaml

  function: visual.count_max
```
