## windows

### `windows.registry_key_exists`

tests if Windows registry key exists (Windows only)

**Use for:** checking an install/config action created a key. Windows guests only (other OSes error). A key that exists but denies read access is an execution error, not a pass.

*QGA_PROBE*, os: windows

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **key_path** | `str` |  | ``HIVE/sub/key`` with ``/`` or ``\`` separators. Hive is case-insensitive: ``HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT``/``HKCR``, ``HKEY_CURRENT_USER``/``HKCU``, ``HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE``/``HKLM``, ``HKEY_USERS``/``HKU``, ``HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG``/``HKCC``. A bare hive or unknown hive is an execution error. HKCU is the agent's user. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_registry_key_exists
  function: windows.registry_key_exists
  parameter:
    key_path: <str>
```

### `windows.registry_value_matches`

tests if Windows registry value matches expected value (Windows only)

**Use for:** asserting a setting/MRU value written by an application. Windows only. A missing key or value fails.

*QGA_PROBE*, os: windows

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **key_path** | `str` |  | ``HIVE/sub/key`` (see windows.registry_key_exists), ``/`` or ``\`` separators. |
| **value_name** | `str` |  | Name of the value; ``''`` selects the key's default value. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| bytes` |  | Compared with Python ``==`` against the ``winreg`` data, so the type matters: REG_DWORD/QWORD -> int, REG_SZ/REG_EXPAND_SZ -> str (unexpanded), REG_BINARY -> bytes. REG_MULTI_SZ (a list) can never match. A ``{{ }}`` placeholder still present at run time is resolved, and all-digit results become int. |
| value_type | `str \| None` | `None` | Optional type name check, case-insensitive, e.g. ``REG_SZ``. REG_DWORD values are reported as ``REG_DWORD_LITTLE_ENDIAN`` and REG_QWORD as ``UNKNOWN_TYPE_11``, so use those strings (``REG_DWORD`` never matches). ``None`` skips the check. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_registry_value_matches
  function: windows.registry_value_matches
  parameter:
    key_path: <str>
    value_name: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | bytes>
```

## xml

### `xml.attribute_matches`

tests if XML element attribute matches expected value with regex and timestamp tolerance support

**Use for:** asserting attribute values (an id, a state, a timestamp ...). No matching element or a missing attribute fails.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. |
| **attribute** | `str` |  | Attribute name; namespaced attributes need the ``{uri}name`` form. |
| **expected_value** | `str` |  | Exact expected value, or a regex with ``regex_match``; a single ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag is matched by type. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares lower-cased / uses ``re.IGNORECASE``. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_attribute_matches
  function: xml.attribute_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    attribute: <str>
    expected_value: <str>
```

### `xml.element_count`

tests the number of XML elements matching XPath expression

**Use for:** counting entries; ``expected_count: 0`` asserts absence (opposite of xml.element_exists).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Required non-negative integer to compare against; anything else is an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``; other values are an error. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_element_count
  function: xml.element_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `xml.element_exists`

tests if XML element exists at specified XPath

**Use for:** checking a config/profile XML gained an entry. For "absent" use xml.element_count with ``expected_count: 0``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_element_exists
  function: xml.element_exists
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
```

### `xml.element_text_matches`

tests if XML element text content matches expected value with placeholder support for regex and timestamp tolerance

**Use for:** asserting an XML setting or record value, and document properties of office files: the author of a .docx is ``dc:creator`` in ``report.docx!/docProps/core.xml`` (xpath ``./dc:creator``, namespaces ``{dc: 'http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/'}``). "Text" is ``element.text``: only the text before the element's first child, not stripped (missing -> ``''``). To count elements use xml.element_count.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. No match fails. |
| **expected_value** | `str` |  | Required. Exact expected text (``''`` for an empty element), or a regex with ``regex_match``. A single ``!re``/``!timestamp`` tag is matched by type (``case_sensitive`` then ignored); an invalid regex is an error. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Search ``expected_value`` as a Python regex (``re.search``, unanchored). |
| case_sensitive | `bool` | `True` | ``False`` compares lower-cased / uses ``re.IGNORECASE``. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | For several matched elements: ``any`` (default) or ``all`` must match; other values are an execution error (only checked when several elements match). |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_element_text_matches
  function: xml.element_text_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    expected_value: <str>
```

### `xml.namespace_matches`

tests if XML namespace declarations match expected namespaces

**Use for:** checking which XML dialect/schema version a file uses. Only the root element's own namespace is detected, under prefix ``''``: ElementTree drops ``xmlns:*`` attributes, so other declared prefixes are never seen and expecting them fails.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| expected_namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Required map prefix -> URI, e.g. ``{'': 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'}``; ``None`` is an execution error. |
| check_mode | `str` | `'contains'` | ``contains`` (default; every expected prefix present with that URI) or ``exact`` (dicts equal). Other values are an execution error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_namespace_matches
  function: xml.namespace_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `xml.xpath_result_matches`

tests if XPath expression result matches expected value (text, number, or boolean)

**Use for:** typed checks on the first matched element. Prefer xml.element_text_matches for text.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool` |  | Required. Converted per ``result_type``: ``str()``, ``float()`` or ``bool()``. Note ``bool('false')`` is True -- use unquoted YAML ``true``/``false``. |
| result_type | `str` | `'text'` | ``text`` (default; first element's ``.text``, ``''`` if none), ``number`` (``float`` of that text; no match -> 0.0, non-numeric -> execution error) or ``boolean`` (whether anything matched). Other values are an execution error. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_xpath_result_matches
  function: xml.xpath_result_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool>
```

## yaml

### `yaml.contains_key`

tests if a YAML file contains the specified key path (supports several documents)

**Use for:** checking that a settings/config file gained a key. To also check the value use yaml.value_matches; to check that a key is absent use yaml.value_count with ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` here: a missing file stays an error).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file (read with ``safe_load``; UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a BOM). A glob must match exactly one path; ``archive.zip!/member.yaml`` reads an archive member. A missing, unreadable or invalid file is an error. A file with several documents (``---``) is a top-level list, one per document; an empty file has no keys. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root, e.g. ``display.font.size``. ``*`` expands all values of a mapping, ``name[*]`` all elements of sequence ``name``, ``name[0]`` / ``name[-1]`` one element; a leading ``[0]`` / ``[*]`` addresses a top-level sequence or a document of a multi-document file (``[1].kind``, ``[*].kind``). Keys with dots use quotes in brackets (``['app.window'].width``). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: yaml.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `yaml.value_count`

tests how many YAML values exist at a key path, optionally only those matching a value (0 = absent)

**Use for:** counting entries (``recent[*]``, documents ``[*]``) and asserting absence: ``expected_count: 0`` passes when the key path selects nothing (or nothing matches ``expected_value``), while a missing or invalid file is still an error. A path that selects one sequence counts its elements when ``expected_value`` is given; without it every selected value counts once.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file; a glob must match exactly one path. Several documents form a top-level list; an empty file has no values. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root (syntax as in yaml.contains_key). |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare with. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Only count values equal to this (normalised as in yaml.value_matches). ``None`` (default) counts every value. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched in ``str(value)``. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: yaml.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `yaml.value_matches`

tests if the YAML value at a key path matches the expected value (supports wildcards with any/all modes)

**Use for:** asserting a setting/field value. If the path yields several values (a wildcard, or a sequence value, whose elements are then compared one by one) ``wildcard_mode`` decides. Values keep their YAML 1.1 types (``5`` is an int, ``true``/``yes``/``on`` and ``false``/``no``/``off`` are booleans); dates and timestamps become ISO 8601 strings (``2024-01-15``, ``2024-01-15T10:30:00``, ``+00:00`` for a ``Z`` zone), ``!!binary`` a lowercase hex string.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file; a glob must match exactly one path. Several documents form a top-level list. A missing or invalid file is an error; an unresolvable key path fails. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root (syntax as in yaml.contains_key), e.g. ``servers[*].port`` or ``[0].kind`` for the first document. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` |  | Compared with Python ``==``, which is type-sensitive (``5`` != ``"5"``; ``null`` needs ``null``). A ``!re`` tag (``re.match``) or ``{{placeholder}}`` compares ``str(value)``. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``. An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default): one value must match; ``all``: every value must match. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: yaml.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | None>
```
